sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from respondents on account of death of Swamy N., husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.2 and 3 and son of petitioner No.4, in Road Traffic Accident.

2. In brief, petition averments are; that on 11-11- 2019 at about 12.30 p.m., Swamy N., was driving Indica Car, bearing No.KA-04-AA-7927 along with inmate Akanksha Gupta on B.B. Road, Venkatala flyover, Yelahanka i.e., from Devanahalli towards Bengaluru carefully, cautiously and observing all traffic rules

, at that time Ritz Car, bearing No.KA-02-ME-7736 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life came from behind and dashed against the Indica Car.

Resulting in which the Indica Car was crossed the centre median and entered into the Bengaluru-Devanahalli road, at the same time BBMP Garbage Lorry, bearing No.KA-01-AG-0678 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life came from Bengaluru towards Devanahalli and dashed against the 4 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 Indica Car.
Due to the impact, Swamy N., sustained severe head injury and other injuries all over the body and died on the spot.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as car driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, on account of his untimely death petitioners lost the dependency, love and affection.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
3. Respondent No.4 remained absent and therefore, it was placed exparte.

3(a). In brief, the objections by respondent No.1 to 3 are that;
3(b).

Respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Maruti-Ritz Car and its validity as on the date of accident and denied the other petition averments generally and it contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6)
of M.V. Act, petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of motor car, bearing No.KA-04-AA-7927 are not made as parties, respondent No.2 entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drove the same as on the date of accident, the driver of car, bearing No.KA-04-AA-7927 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and crossed centre median and entered into the opposite track and dashed against BBMP Lorry,
bearing No.KA-01- 5 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 AG-678 and caused the accident, there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver insured vehicle and deceased was driven the car in rash and negligent manner without having driving licence, insurance and not wearing safety seat belt at the time of accident.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

3(c). Respondent No.2 admitted the ownership in respect of Ritz Car, bearing No.KA-02-ME-7736,
possession of valid driving licence and insurance policy with respondent No.1 and policy was in force as on the date of accident, he was driving the car from Devanahalli towards Bengaluru slowly,
carefully and cautiously by observing all traffic rules, when he reached B.B. Road, Venkatala flyover,

Further, he contended that the said accident was caused solely due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Indica Car and BBMP Garbage Lorry.

For the above denials and contentions he prayed for dismissal of the petition.
3(d). Respondent No.3 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of BBMP Garbage Lorry and its validity as on the date of accident and denied the other petition averments generally and it contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6)
of M.V. Act, the driver of its insured vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drove the same as on the date of accident.

As without prejudice, it contended that the alleged accident was taken place due to careless and negligence on the part of the driver of car, bearing No.KA-02-ME-7736 who was driving his car in a rash and negligent manner, without observing moving vehicles and dashed against car, bearing No.KA-04-AA-7927, due to which the said driver lost control over his vehicle and dashed against to the road divider and got entered into the opposite road and dashed to lorry, bearing No.KA- 01-AG-0678 which was moving on the left side of the road.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.4 under Section 170 of the 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that Swamy N., succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have occurred on 11-11-2019 at about 12.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of Ritz Car, bearing registration No.KA-02-ME- 7736 and BBMP Garbage Lorry, bearing No.KA-01-AG-0678?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

sentences.text: 6. Heard the counsel for petitioners and respondent No.1 and 3.

No arguments by respondent No.2.
Perused the pleadings and evidences, on the basis, findings on the issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following REASONS ISSUE No.1:
7.
Petitioners, respondent No.1 and 3 led their oral as well as documentary evidences.
Respondent No.2 remained neutral.
Respondent No.4 remained exparte.
This is a summary proceedings, so, a sum and substance of the pleadings and evidences are only emphasized.
The petitioners need to prove this issue on preponderance of probability as test for proof is preponderance of probability herein.
The petition averments and objections are summarized herein above in the brief facts of case and objections, those are not repeated in avoidance of repetition.
Respondent No.1 to 3 disputed the negligence.
The incident, involvement of vehicles, injuries and death, insurance policies and validity are not in dispute.

8. Regarding the negligence is concerned the petitioners relied on police records viz., true copy of FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, IMV reports, 9 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 notices issued under Section 133 of M.V. Act and reply on the notices, inquest, postmortem report and charge sheet, which are marked in Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
9.

The charge sheet/final report filed by the Yelahanka Traffic Police shows the negligence on the part of the driver of Ritz car, bearing No.KA-02-ME-7736 and BBMP Garbage lorry, bearing No.KA-01-AG-0678, the brief facts of the final report are extracted hereunder for better appreciation:

10. The spot mahazar and sketch depict the scene of occurrence.
The IMV reports show the damages of three vehicles involved in the incident; the reports show that there were no mechanical defects in the vehicles.
Postmortem report shows the cause of death was due to head injury due to road traffic accident.
That, there were no mechanical defects in the vehicles in the sense then the incident was due to the negligence only; it is to be seen that whose negligence was there to the incident.
No eyewitness is examined herein.

On the available 11 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 materials it is found that there was the negligence by both Ritz car, bearing No.KA-02-ME-7736 and BBMP lorry,
bearing No.KA-01-AG-0678.
The charge sheet/final report corroborates the negligence.

Respondent No.2 in his written statement of objection stated that, "the driver of this vehicle in order to avoid any untoward incident suddenly applied the brake and due to which he lost control over the vehicle and as a result of which the vehicle of this respondent has touched the Indica car from its behind as a result of which the said Indica car was crossed the center median and entered into the Bengaluru-Devanahalli road, at the same time, one BBMP garbage lorry, bearing No.KA-01-AG-0678 which was driven by its driver at high speed, rashly and negligently,
endangering to human life came from Bengaluru side towards Devanahalli dashed against the Indica car; as a result the inmates of Indica car were sustained injuries" takes away the voluntary say of RW2 as '      ' in her cross-examination made by petitioner side and fortifies the incident as found by the concerned Investigating Officer in his investigation.
If the Ritz car could not have been hit the deceased's car and if the BBMP lorry could have avoided the incident could not have been occurred.
Here is no acceptable contrary evidence by respondent No.1 and 3.
Hence, here is no impediment in believing the police records regarding the negligence.
Hence those are considered.
The negligence is 12 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 considered at 50:50 ratio on both the drivers of the Ritz car and BBMP lorry.

11. Regarding objections by respondent No.1 and 3 as to non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act is concerned as the petition reached its finality and the petitioners approached the Tribunal, respondent No.1 and 3 had already taken all the contentions of respondent No.2 and 4 the giving of permission under Section 170 of MV Act, and discussion on the same now does not arise.

12. Wherefore, for the foregoing reasons, it establishes on preponderance of probability that Swamy N., succumbed to the injuries and died in vehicular accident occurred on 11-11-2019 at about 12.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of Ritz car, bearing No.KA-02-ME-7736 and BBMP garbage lorry, bearing No.KA-01-AG-0678.
Hence, this issue is answered affirmatively.

6 ISSUE No.2:
13.
In determination of this issue avocation, income, age of the deceased, dependency and future prospects and other conventional heads for compensation are need to be ascertained.
MVC 7287/2019 Avocation :
It is averred that the deceased was working as driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In substantiation of the same the petitioners have not produced any documents except driving licence-Ex.P14.
Hence, no other option but to consider notional income of the deceased in the present case.

Age: 
As per Ex.P10-aadhar card and Ex.P14-driving licence, date of birth of the deceased was 28-12-1985 and so that age of the deceased was 34 years at the time of incident.
Hence, they are considered.
Income:
As discussed on the head of avocation, the deceased's avocation taken to be considered notionally.
In this regard as per the resolution of hon'ble the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, dated 17-02- 2022 notional income for the year 2019 came to be fixed at 14,000/.
In the present case, under the facts and circumstances of the case, Rs.14,000/- is taken to be considered as notional income of the deceased per month.
Dependency:
As per the petition averments petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are children and petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased.
The dependency is not 14 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 in dispute.
Ex. P10
to Ex .P13
, Ex.P15 and Ex.P16 - aadhar cards and birth certificate prove the identification of the petitioners.
Whereas, for deduction of personal expenses is concerned only 1/4th is considered to be deducted in the monthly notional income, for the personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Future prospects:

The future prospects is concerned, the age of the deceased at the time of the death was 34 years, so as per the principle laid down in Hem Raj vs. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others case, reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (SC), 40% needs to be added to the monthly notional income of the deceased.

entities.text: Hem Raj vs. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, 40% is added to the monthly income of the deceased.
Thus, 40% of addition will come to Rs.5,600/-.

In total, the monthly Jancy R vs The Manager on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174946038/
7 notional income will be Rs.19,600/-.
Conventional Heads:

As conventional heads, the deceased being husband of petitioner No.1 spousal consortium, father of petitioner No.2 and 3 parental consortium and son of petitioner No.4 filial consortium are to be considered as the petitioners suffered the loss of love and affection.

Hence, in view of the observations made, in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others, in civil Appeal 15 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 No.2705/2020, by hon'ble Apex Court, Rs.40,000/- each is considered to be awarded as compensation for consortium respectively.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The loss of estate is concerned, as the deceased was with the family, if the incident could not have been occurred, he could have been contributed more or less from his savings to the estate of the family; the incident caused such loss to the estate of the petitioners.
Hence, Rs.15,000/- is need to be awarded on this head as the principle laid down by hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, and others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, and others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Likewise, for the funeral expenses is concerned awarding of Rs.15,000/- is also just under the conventional head as observed by hon'ble the Apex Court.
Hence, it is considered to be awarded.

14. Accordingly, compensation is calculated as under;
Monthly notional income of Rs.14,000/-.
Future prospects in 40% on the monthly notional income is Rs.5,600/-.
Monthly notional income + future prospects = 19,600/-.
For personal and living expenses, after the deduction of 1/4th, the total monthly notional income is Rs.14,700/-.

Net monthly notional income is Rs.14,700/- is calculated to net annul income as Rs.14,700/- x 12 which is = 1,76,400/-.
16 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 Multiplier is 16.

Net annual notional income is multiplied by multiplier 16, which is as Rs.1,76,400/- x 16, will come to Rs.28,22,400/-.
15.
So, compensation for loss of dependency is found at Rs.28,22,400/- plus compensation on conventional heads, such as spousal, parental and filial consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

16. The details of compensation proposed to be awarded are as under:

In all, petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.30,12,400/-.

Keeping in view the interest on the savings by the nationalized banks and as provided under Section 34 of the CPC, in the present case, from the date of petition only the interest at 6% per annum is considered to be directed till its realization.
So, the petitioners are entitled to the interest at 6% per annum on the compensation amount.
17 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 Liability:
18. Insurance policies and their validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurers.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the drivers of the Ritz car and BBMP garbage lorry.
On vicarious liability respondent No.2 and 4 being the owners are responsible, respondent No.1 and 3 being the insurers of respondent No.2 and 4 contractually liable to pay compensation.
Thus, respondent No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.1 and 3 are equally liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioners are only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
19.
In view of the findings on issue No.1 and 2, the petition deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence,
the following order is passed:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.30,12,400/- (Rupees thirty lakhs,
twelve thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate 18 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is -Insurance Companies equally and they were directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Act, petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of motor car, bearing No.KA-04-AA-7927 are not made as parties, respondent No.2 entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drove the same as on the date of accident, the driver of car, bearing No.KA-04-AA-7927 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and crossed centre median and entered into the opposite track and dashed against BBMP Lorry,
bearing No.KA-01- 5 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 AG-678 and caused the accident, there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver insured vehicle and deceased was driven the car in rash and negligent manner without having driving licence, insurance and not wearing safety seat belt at the time of accident.
Further, he contended that the said accident was caused solely due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Indica Car and BBMP Garbage Lorry.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.4 under Section 170 of the 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 M.V. Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that Swamy N., succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have occurred on 11-11-2019 at about 12.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of Ritz Car, bearing registration No.KA-02-ME- 7736 and BBMP Garbage Lorry, bearing No.KA-01-AG-0678?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
5.
12. Wherefore, for the foregoing reasons, it establishes on preponderance of probability that Swamy N., succumbed to the injuries and died in vehicular accident occurred on 11-11-2019 at about 12.30 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of Ritz car, bearing No.KA-02-ME-7736 and BBMP garbage lorry, bearing No.KA-01-AG-0678.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
If the Ritz car could not have been hit the deceased's car and if the BBMP lorry could have avoided the incident could not have been occurred.
The negligence is 12 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 considered at 50:50 ratio on both the drivers of the Ritz car and BBMP lorry.
In the present case, under the facts and circumstances of the case, Rs.14,000/- is taken to be considered as notional income of the deceased per month.
As per the petition averments petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are children and petitioner No.4 is mother of the deceased.
The dependency is not 14 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 in dispute.
As conventional heads, the deceased being husband of petitioner No.1 spousal consortium, father of petitioner No.2 and 3 parental consortium and son of petitioner No.4 filial consortium are to be considered as the petitioners suffered the loss of love and affection.
Hence, in view of the observations made, in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others, in civil Appeal 15 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 No.2705/2020, by hon'ble Apex Court, Rs.40,000/- each is considered to be awarded as compensation for consortium respectively.
The loss of estate is concerned, as the deceased was with the family, if the incident could not have been occurred, he could have been contributed more or less from his savings to the estate of the family; the incident caused such loss to the estate of the petitioners.
On vicarious liability respondent No.2 and 4 being the owners are responsible, respondent No.1 and 3 being the insurers of respondent No.2 and 4 contractually liable to pay compensation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
14. Accordingly, compensation is calculated as under;
Monthly notional income of Rs.14,000/-.
In all, petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.30,12,400/-.
So, the petitioners are entitled to the interest at 6% per annum on the compensation amount.
Thus, respondent No.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.1 and 3 are equally liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioners are only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.
ISSUE No.3:
19.
In view of the findings on issue No.1 and 2, the petition deserves to be allowed in part.
Hence,
the following order is passed:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.30,12,400/- (Rupees thirty lakhs,
twelve thousand and four hundred only) with interest at the rate 18 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is -Insurance Companies equally and they were directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Compensation amount is Jancy R vs The Manager on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174946038/
9  apportioned as follows:-
 Petitioner No.1 - Wife 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - Daughter 15%
 Petitioner No.3 - Son 15%
 Petitioner No.4 - Mother 20%
 Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner No.1 and 4, 25% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names as FD in any nationalized bank for the period of two years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 75% amount with proportionate interest shall be released to them through E- 19 (SCCH-16) MVC 7287/2019 payment on proper identification and verification.
Out of the compensation amount so apportioned in favour of the petitioner Nos.2 and 3 being the minors, entire compensation amount shall be deposited in the name of minor petitioners as FD in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner No.1 till they attain majority.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
